**Security: pass-with-notes** at `516523b6f1d773c9902b597c5b38ccc03e4f9417`.

F127 closes the targeted mint-time seat-ID and PA-digest rendering paths. It does **not** close all daemon-authored messages containing caller-chosen metadata or prose. No newly introduced exploitable authority-laundering path or C19/C21 disclosure was established.

## Remaining source-derived exposures

All three findings below are **preexisting, unchanged sinks**, nonblocking for this additions-only PR. They are not accepted because of F88: each can use the caller's own identity. Structured senders remain correct; the exposure is forged model-facing authorship/instruction framing. No successful malicious model action or direct execution was demonstrated.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| 1 | 🟡 MEDIUM | crates/daemon/src/delivery/role_send.rs | 755-795 | Caller-chosen request ID remains raw in immediate daemon-authored role-queue wakes and related notices | 9/10 |
| 2 | 🟡 MEDIUM | crates/core/src/watchdog.rs | 834-859 | Raw model telemetry enters daemon-authored large-seat FYIs | 8/10 |
| 3 | 🟡 MEDIUM | crates/daemon/src/http/output.rs | 482-501 | Nonempty but non-SHA/newline-capable output head remains raw in generated notifications | 8/10 |

1. A local admitted sender can choose a request ID containing newlines or forged `[pij from]` framing, then send to an existing role with no live holder. The ID is stored from `send.msg_id`; its admission checks `@`, not the digest grammar. `wake_body` interpolates it into the immediate queue wake, and `wake_pa` supplies the real `pij-bg` sender. F127 protects the digest's copy, not this message, the holder frame or time-limit notices.
2. A caller controls its own seat's model report/fallback, belongs to a watched fleet and crosses the large-context threshold. If native model facts do not supersede that value, `large_seats_body` renders it raw in a prime FYI. This does not require another seat's context grant or identity.
3. A valid output writer can provide framing in `head`: the validator requires a verdict head to be nonempty, not a SHA or one line (`crates/daemon/src/community/output.rs:74-105`). The generated notice retains the writer as sender; it still permits textual claims of another author in the body.

The common Copilot native sink JSON-quotes the real header fields but appends the already-rendered body unchanged (`.copilot/extensions/pij/store.mjs:1970-1974`). Header quoting does not contain metadata interpolated into that body earlier.

## Targeted controls verified

`SeatId::is_canonical` fully consumes the ASCII `pij-`/lowercase-alphanumeric-word grammar with single hyphens and a 64-byte cap. The mint-time refusal bounds and debug-escapes the rejected value (`crates/core/src/model.rs:30-73`).

Ordinary/native/paneless/reclaim registration converges on the new-mint check; existing/prebound targets retain their own descriptor identity. Explicit spawn IDs are checked before lookup/launch. Adoption still refuses caller-supplied IDs; binders use registration. Legacy revive remains compatible, not a new mint. Closed asserted-role checks remain intact at HTTP, placement and store boundaries.

The digest guards every seat-ID, asserted-role, message-ID and request-ID occurrence at render time, including stored rows (`crates/core/src/pa_digest.rs:139-162,175-319`). Invalid values become only `invalid (N chars)`; lookup/delivery use the original identity, not that placeholder. The #175 canonical build/tree renderer and its length caps remain unchanged.

`SeatId::Display` is still raw (`model.rs:84-87`), so `rendered()` is opt-in. Admission is not a blanket proof that legacy values in other generated messages are safe.

## What else remains raw

| Field or message family | Remaining boundary and source |
|---|---|
| PA headline scope | Repository/folder-derived scope is raw; it requires control of the scope anchor/resolved path, not merely an arbitrary worker folder. `crates/core/src/pa_digest.rs:175-183`; `crates/daemon/src/pa_watchdog.rs:1090-1139`. |
| Digest anomaly kind/detail | Raw at `crates/core/src/pa_digest.rs:195-209`. Current producers are narrower: numeric stale age, fixed receiver-expiry text, parsed build/tree and adapter tap errors. No arbitrary caller-set tap-detail exploit established. |
| Digest queued address/project | Community role/instance/project strings are not render-validated. Current role-send word grammar and existing project slug selection constrain producers, not arbitrary malformed stored rows. Request bodies are **not** included in the automatic digest. |
| Cards, status lines and notes | `did`/`next` are capped at 280 characters, notes at 200, with line-separator rejection/whitespace collapsing. They remain untrusted prose in receipts/state/card responses, **not automatic PA-digest content**; stale-card digest text is age only. `crates/daemon/src/http/report.rs:321-356`. Model status/fallback has the separate FYI exposure above. |
| Other watchdog/presence messages | Legacy IDs, roles, setter and receipt text still render outside `digest()`. Current mint/role grammars narrow new values; surrounding prose is not protected by shell-word quoting. `crates/core/src/watchdog.rs:92-96,431-446,770-859`. |
| Request frames, close/withdrawal and limit notices | IDs, reasons and original request bodies remain raw. Bodies are intentional free text; actor/requester provenance must remain explicit, not be treated as daemon policy. `crates/daemon/src/delivery/role_send.rs:550-565,1535-1544,1596-1617`; `crates/daemon/src/http/requests.rs:494-514`; `crates/daemon/src/http/directory.rs:1130-1159`. |
| Output metadata and stored prose | Subject rejects CR/LF and verdict result is closed, but head, answers and non-verdict result are not all closed metadata. Body/notes/evidence/link are stored for later reading, not copied into the generated notice. |
| Background output/event turns | Titles have a 120-unit cap and CR/LF/NUL rejection; tails are 1,200 characters with lines flattened; event inline/batch data is size-limited. Job/source instructions and other controls are not thereby sanitized. `crates/daemon/src/background.rs:1129-1142,1701-1771`. |
| Holding/claim memory and compaction text | Roles/projects have constrained producers, but holding instances reject only slash and edge whitespace, not internal newlines/controls. These values still enter generated prompts/commands. `crates/daemon/src/http/directory.rs:1433-1442`; `crates/daemon/src/http/memory_turn.rs:122-128,399-430`; `crates/core/src/compaction_wake.rs:94-116`. |
| Baton, dispatch and decision text | Purpose, packet path and answers remain workflow/free-text content. Packet hashes bind bytes, not the authority of prose. Structured requester/actor sender is retained. `crates/daemon/src/http/governance.rs:1386-1389,1786-1801`; `crates/daemon/src/http/decisions.rs:243-250`. |
| Usage-reset quota type | Transcript-derived `rateLimitType` remains unrestricted text in a generated wake; no arbitrary HTTP setter established. `crates/core/src/usage_limit.rs:58-64,171-192`. |
| Modal notices | Captured pane prose is **not** exported: dialog labels/keys/clears are closed classifier output. Legacy raw seat IDs in other notices remain the qualification above. `crates/core/src/modal_stall.rs:145-154`. |

Follow-up should apply closed metadata rendering across these authored-message families and preserve the explicitly untrusted origin of intentional free-text payloads. Do not advertise this patch as blanket prompt-injection closure. Invalid-value character counting also scans the rejected string; this verdict does not certify constant-cost rendering for arbitrarily large legacy/message-ID values.

## Evidence and limits

Local and GitHub heads agree; worktree clean; PR CLEAN and ready; all five checks succeeded. CI [42454424975](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42454424975) tested synthetic merge `6ea7fdc`, incorporating this exact head.

JUnit artifact [13607366481](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42454424975/artifacts/13607366481) confirms 2,215 passing cases, with five separately skipped. Executed controls cover every memorable generated ID, hostile ID grammar, hostile stored digest fields, new-mint rejection, forged IDs/roles at entry points and all closed-role setters. These independently prove guard execution; author-reported killed mutants are not independent mutation proof. The new digest test is a core renderer fixture, not a new hostile native-delivery canary.

No local cargo/builds/tests/scripts or hostile reproductions, credentials, edits, actual daemon/delivery/PA operations or pane/process probes. All remaining exposure assessments are source-derived.
